CHATBOTS.name: ChatGPT
CHATBOTS.blurb: All-rounder for writing, coding and ideas.
CHATBOTS.brief: Unlimited text chat; uploads and tools capped.
CHATBOTS.best: Versatile all-rounder for writing, brainstorming, coding, explaining concepts and varied tasks. Most widely used.
CHATBOTS.free: Text chat has no message cap (default model GPT-5.6 Luna since Aug 2026, abuse limits apply); a free account adds history and tools. Uploads, image generation, Deep Research, voice and Codex have small quotas, and free users may see ads.

CHATBOTS.name: Gemini
CHATBOTS.brief: Free Google account; heavy tools have daily caps.
CHATBOTS.best: Best if you live in Google Workspace; strong at multimodal work with text, images and other media.
CHATBOTS.free: Needs a free Google account. Free use is mostly on Auto / Flash-class models with a smaller context window. Deep Research, images and extended reasoning have daily caps; video generation is paid.

CHATBOTS.name: Claude
CHATBOTS.blurb: Long documents, careful writing and code.
CHATBOTS.brief: Free account; 5-hour and weekly usage windows.
CHATBOTS.best: Long documents, careful writing, summarization, coding and analysis of complex material.
CHATBOTS.free: Needs a free account. Usage runs on a rolling 5-hour window plus a weekly cap, and long pastes use it up faster. Artifacts, file creation, web search, memory and up to 5 Projects are included; Research and Claude Code are paid.

CHATBOTS.name: Perplexity
CHATBOTS.brief: Works signed out; deep research is capped.
CHATBOTS.best: AI search engine for web research; answers usually include source citations. Keep prompts short.
CHATBOTS.free: Basic search is unlimited and works signed out; a free account adds history. Pro Search is a few a day (reports say 3 to 5) and Deep Research is small or inconsistent; image generation and model choice need Pro. Reports disagree, so check the app.

CHATBOTS.name: Grok
CHATBOTS.brief: Tight message limits; some features need sign-in.
CHATBOTS.best: Conversational assistant tied to X (Twitter); good for exploring current topics and discussions.
CHATBOTS.free: Free daily access with limited Chat, Imagine, Grok Build and DeepSearch (xAI publishes no fixed numbers; about 10 prompts per 2 hours is reported). Full Imagine video, DeeperSearch and Tasks need a paid plan.

CHATBOTS.name: Microsoft Copilot
CHATBOTS.blurb: Windows and Edge users; a free fallback bot.
CHATBOTS.brief: Free; sign in for history and uploads.
CHATBOTS.best: Easily accessible on Windows and Edge, with free web answers, image generation and deeper reasoning modes. Useful as a fallback when another chatbot hits its free usage cap.
CHATBOTS.free: Free to use. Think Deeper is free (Microsoft says use is not limited, though paid Microsoft 365 users get priority at busy times). Signing in with a Microsoft account is recommended for history and uploads. Deep Research and image creation have small allowances that change.

CHATBOTS.name: DeepSeek
CHATBOTS.blurb: Free reasoning, coding and maths help.
CHATBOTS.brief: Free account; no paid chat plan.
CHATBOTS.best: Widely noted for generous free chat and reasoning, and for coding and maths help. A good pick when data sensitivity is not a blocker: check its privacy policy and keep confidential or personal material out of it.
CHATBOTS.free: Free with an account; there is no paid chat plan and no published daily cap, though busy periods can slow it down. DeepThink (reasoning) and Search are switches under the message box. It cannot generate images.

CHATBOTS.name: Meta AI
CHATBOTS.blurb: Quick everyday prompts in WhatsApp and Instagram.
CHATBOTS.brief: Free; paid Meta One adds usage (limited testing).
CHATBOTS.best: Convenient if you already live inside WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger: quick everyday questions, casual writing and image ideas without opening another app. Lighter on long documents and deep analysis.
CHATBOTS.free: Free for everyday use in Meta apps and at meta.ai; heavier image and video generation has unpublished daily and monthly limits. Paid Meta One plans (Core $7.99, Premium $19.99) add usage but are in limited testing and vary by account. Prompts may be used to improve Meta AI, so check privacy settings.

free: Works on the free plan with no special quota worry.
account: Free, but you must be signed in to a free account.
limited: Free users get a small daily or monthly allowance. Save it for tasks that need it.
paid: Not available on free plans (or only a taste of it). Skip it on a free account.

BOT_NOTES.ChatGPT: ChatGPT mixes typed commands (/ and @) with a + tools menu. The typed commands are shortcuts whose availability depends on the app and version, so if one does not appear, use the + menu instead. A free account is needed for uploads and history, and several tools have small free quotas. Agent mode is paid.
BOT_NOTES.Gemini: Gemini has no slash commands and needs a free Google account. It uses a Tools menu, and @ to call a Connected App. Google Maps, YouTube, Flights and Hotels are used automatically when you ask (the old @Google Maps style mentions were retired). Video generation is paid.
BOT_NOTES.Claude: Claude needs a free account. Its chat has no typed slash commands: typing / just opens the same menu as the + button (Claude Code, the developer tool, is different). Most control is by switches in that menu or by asking in words. File creation and connectors work on free accounts, but free usage limits are tight, so keep pastes short; Research is paid.
BOT_NOTES.Perplexity: Perplexity treats every message as a search and has no slash commands. You steer it with the Search mode menu and the sources picker. Free users get unlimited basic searches, a few Pro Searches a day and little or no deep research (reports disagree, so check the menu). Older guides call the source picker Focus; the name differs by app version.
BOT_NOTES.Grok: Grok has no slash commands. Switches sit under the message box on grok.com and in the apps, and newer Grok models may reason automatically. Free access has tight limits; DeeperSearch, Imagine video and Tasks need a paid plan.
BOT_NOTES.Microsoft Copilot: Copilot has no slash commands. You steer it with the mode selector under the message box (Smart, Quick response, Think Deeper, Study and Learn, Search) and a separate Deep Research option. Mode names and places differ between Windows, Edge, the web and the app, so pick the closest match. Free use is generous; Deep Research and image creation have small allowances.
BOT_NOTES.DeepSeek: DeepSeek has no slash commands. Under the message box you pick Instant or Expert Mode and switch DeepThink (reasoning) and Search on or off. It needs a free account, cannot generate images and has no paid chat plan. Avoid confidential or personal material.
BOT_NOTES.Meta AI: Meta AI has no slash commands. In WhatsApp or Messenger group chats you call it by typing @Meta AI, and Imagine creates images. The Meta AI app and meta.ai add voice and, where offered, a Thinking option. Features vary by country and app, and paid Meta One plans (Core, Premium) exist but are only in limited testing.

ChatGPT.d: Starts Deep Research: ChatGPT proposes a research plan you can edit, browses many sources (web, your files, connected apps) and returns a cited report. Best for multi-source questions, market scans and literature reviews; overkill for quick facts. Free users get only a few lighter reports per month.

ChatGPT.w: Type / and choose Search, or + menu > Search the web
ChatGPT.d: Forces a live web search with cited sources instead of answering from training data. Use it for anything recent: news, prices, rules, product specs.
Study mode: ChatGPT asks guiding questions and works through the problem with you instead of handing over the answer. Not available in Temporary Chats, GPTs or Projects.

f: App or plugin name (e.g. Google Drive)
ChatGPT.w: Type @ then the app name, or + menu > pick the app
ChatGPT.d: Points ChatGPT at one connected app or plugin so it searches or acts there (find a file, summarise a thread). Connect the app first in settings; free-plan app access is limited. Put the task in your core prompt.
Switches ChatGPT to image generation. Describe subject, style, lighting, aspect ratio and any text that must appear. Free users have a small daily image allowance.

ChatGPT.t: Use agent mode: carry out this task step by step in a browser, and ask me before any purchase, login or irreversible action.
ChatGPT.d: ChatGPT operates a virtual browser to complete multi-step tasks such as gathering data across sites or filling forms. It should pause for your confirmation on sensitive steps.

ChatGPT.t: Open this in canvas, the editable side panel, so I can revise it directly.
ChatGPT.d: A side-by-side editor for long writing or code. You can select text and ask for targeted edits instead of regenerating everything.

ChatGPT.t: Use my connected apps to find the information you need before answering.
ChatGPT.d: Lets ChatGPT read from services you have connected (Drive, Slack, GitHub and similar). Results are limited to what your own account can access, and free-plan connectors are limited.

ChatGPT.t: Take extra time to reason carefully before you answer, and check your work.
ChatGPT.w: Model picker > Thinking (names vary by plan)
ChatGPT.d: Uses ChatGPT's reasoning mode: slower, but stronger on maths, logic, coding and multi-step planning. Free users get a small number of uses.

ChatGPT.t: Use your Python data-analysis tool to calculate, chart or process the data provided, and show the results.
ChatGPT.d: Runs code in ChatGPT's sandbox for calculations, charts, data cleaning and file conversions. Attach the data file to the chat (needs a free account for uploads).

ChatGPT.t: Create a downloadable file (Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF) containing the result.
ChatGPT.d: Asks ChatGPT to build a real file you can download rather than pasting text. Name the file type you want. Free accounts get little or no Office-file creation, so if it only pastes text, copy it into your own app.

f: App (Gmail, Google Drive, Calendar, Docs, Keep, Tasks, Photos, YouTube Music, Spotify...)
Gemini.w: Type @ and select the app; manage in Settings > Personal Intelligence > Connected Apps
Gemini.d: Makes Gemini use one Connected App for this request, for example to find an email, a Drive file or a calendar slot. You must be signed in, and Keep Activity must be on. If the app is not connected yet, Gemini asks permission.

Gemini.t: Run Deep Research on this: make a research plan, browse many sources and write a detailed report with citations.
Gemini.d: Gemini drafts a multi-step plan, searches the web in depth and produces a long cited report. Free users have a small monthly allowance (about 5 reports a month has been reported).

Gemini.t: Use Canvas to build this so I can edit it side by side.
Gemini.d: An interactive workspace for documents and code. Good for drafting, small apps and games with a live preview, quizzes and flashcards.

Gemini.t: Use Guided Learning: teach me step by step with hints and knowledge checks instead of just giving the answer.
Gemini.d: Tutor mode: breaks a topic into steps, asks questions and checks understanding. Upload notes or a textbook page to learn from your own material.
Generates or edits images. Upload a photo and describe the change to edit it. Daily limits apply on free accounts.
Makes a short clip from text or an image using Google's Veo model. Needs a paid plan.
Generates a short audio track from a description. Free allowance is small.

Gemini.t: Reason step by step at maximum depth before answering.
Gemini.w: Model picker (Thinking; Deep Think is on paid plans)
Gemini.d: Selects Gemini's slower reasoning option for hard maths, code and analysis. Free users get a capped number of uses; which options appear depends on your plan.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Use Google Maps to find places, routes and travel times for: {0}
Gemini.d: Pulls places, opening hours, directions and travel times.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Use Google Flights to check options and prices for: {0}
Gemini.d: Finds flight options and fares. It does not book for you.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Use Google Hotels to check options and prices for: {0}
Gemini.d: Finds hotels and prices for your dates.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Use YouTube: find and summarise relevant videos about: {0}
Gemini.d: Finds videos and summarises or answers questions about them.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Turn this material into a quiz with an answer key, plus flashcards.
Gemini.w: No switch: just ask (Canvas shows them as interactive cards)
Gemini.d: Creates practice questions and flashcards from your notes, a document or a topic.

Gemini.g: Ask in words (Gemini uses these Google services itself)
Gemini.t: Create an Audio Overview: a podcast-style discussion of the attached material.
Gemini.d: Turns uploaded documents into a spoken two-host style summary. Free use is capped.

Claude.t: Use Research: investigate this across the web and my connected tools, then write a cited report.
Claude.w: + menu > Research (paid plans; web search must be on)
Claude.d: Claude runs many searches and reads many sources, including connected Google Workspace and other connectors, then writes a cited report. Start it on the web or desktop app to include connectors; mobile uses the web only. Turn off connectors that can write or send first. Not part of free plans.

Claude.t: Think deeply and check your reasoning before giving the final answer.
Claude.w: Model picker > Extended thinking / Effort toggle (newer models decide for themselves with adaptive thinking)
Claude.d: Gives Claude more reasoning time before it answers. Use for hard maths, logic, code, planning and subtle analysis; skip for quick lookups. On newer models Claude decides by itself when to think harder, so the toggle only appears where a model supports it. It uses up free usage limits faster.

f: Style name (Concise, Explanatory, Formal, or your own)
Claude.w: + menu > Use style (create styles in Settings > Styles)
Claude.d: Applies a saved writing style so you do not repeat tone instructions. You can create custom styles from your own writing samples.

Claude.t: Use my connected tools (Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Slack, Notion and others) to find what you need before answering.
Claude.w: + menu > Connectors (set up in Customize > Connectors)
Claude.d: Lets Claude read from, and sometimes act in, services you have connected. Check what each connector may write before enabling. Connectors became available on free accounts in early 2026; which ones you can use still varies.

Claude.t: Search the web for current information and cite your sources.
Claude.w: Automatic now; asking makes your intent explicit
Claude.d: Claude decides on its own when to search. Saying so forces a search and asks for citations; best for quick facts that change.

Claude.t: Create the result as an Artifact (a standalone document, page or app in its own side panel).
Claude.w: Needs Artifacts enabled in Settings > Capabilities
Claude.d: Puts long documents, code, web pages or small tools in a side panel you can edit, copy, download or share. Doc, Slides and Design templates are reported as free.

Claude.t: Create the result as a downloadable {0} file.
Claude.w: Needs code execution and file creation enabled in Settings > Capabilities
Claude.d: Builds a finished Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF file instead of pasting text. It uses more of your free usage limit than plain chat.

Claude.t: Run code to analyse the data and show your calculations.
Claude.w: Needs code execution enabled; attach the data file
Claude.d: Claude runs code to calculate, clean data and make charts, instead of estimating in its head.

Claude.t: Search my past chats for {0} and use what you find.
Claude.w: Needs Search and reference chats enabled in Settings
Claude.d: Pulls earlier conversations into this one so you do not re-explain context. Availability on free accounts may differ.

Perplexity.g: Search modes (Search menu beside the + button)
Perplexity.t: Run Deep Research: search dozens of sources, reason across them and deliver a structured report with citations.
Perplexity.w: Search menu > Deep research (limited reports on Free)
Perplexity.d: Performs many searches, reads many sources and writes a long, cited report in a few minutes. Use for questions you would otherwise research by hand. Free allowance is small and has been cut back in 2026; reports disagree on whether free accounts get any, so check the Search menu.

Perplexity.g: Search modes (Search menu beside the + button)
Perplexity.t: Teach this step by step, checking my understanding as we go.
Perplexity.w: Search menu > Learn step by step
Perplexity.d: A guided tutoring style instead of a single answer.

Perplexity.g: Sources (Connectors menu or Choose sources, set BEFORE you send)
Perplexity.t: Use academic and peer-reviewed sources only (papers and journals) and cite each one.
Perplexity.w: Focus button in the search bar, or + menu > Connectors > Academic (name varies by version; untick Web for papers only)
Perplexity.d: Limits answers to scholarly material. Weak for recent events, so pair it with Web for current topics.

Perplexity.g: Sources (Connectors menu or Choose sources, set BEFORE you send)
Perplexity.t: Use financial sources only (filings, earnings, market data) and cite each one.
Perplexity.d: Focuses on company filings, earnings and market information.

Perplexity.g: Sources (Connectors menu or Choose sources, set BEFORE you send)
Perplexity.t: Answer only from the files I have attached, and say if the files do not contain the answer.
Perplexity.w: Attach files, then choose the Files source
Perplexity.d: Restricts the answer to your uploads instead of the open web. Uploads need a free account and have small daily limits.

Perplexity.t: Cite every claim with a numbered source link, and flag any claim you could not verify.
Perplexity.d: Perplexity cites by default; this tightens it so each claim has a link and unverified claims are flagged.

Perplexity.t: Compare at least three independent sources and say where they disagree.
Perplexity.d: Surfaces conflicts between sources instead of blending them into one answer.

Perplexity.t: Search Reddit, forums and social media discussions on this and summarise the range of opinions with links.
Perplexity.d: Pulls real-user discussion. Treat as anecdotal evidence, not fact.

Perplexity.t: Summarise the most recent news on this, newest first, with dates and links.
Perplexity.d: Real-time news with dates, a core Perplexity strength.

Perplexity.t: Build this as a Perplexity Labs project: a report, dashboard or small web app, with the sources used.
Perplexity.d: Asks for a longer, built deliverable rather than a chat answer. Not part of free plans.

Grok.t: Use DeepSearch: search the web and X thoroughly, follow fresh links, then give a reasoned answer with cited sources.
Grok.w: DeepSearch toggle, or start your message with 'Use DeepSearch:'
Grok.d: An agent that splits your question into sub-searches across the web, X and news, cross-checks them and cites sources. Use for anything time-sensitive. Free users get a few uses per day.

Grok.t: Use DeeperSearch: go deeper than standard DeepSearch, checking more sources and cross-verifying key claims.
Grok.d: A more thorough variant of DeepSearch for research where completeness matters more than speed. Needs a paid plan.

Grok.t: Think step by step before answering and show your reasoning.
Grok.w: Think toggle (newer Grok models may reason automatically, with no toggle)
Grok.d: Switches on Grok's reasoning path for multi-step maths, logic and decisions. Turn it off for plain summarising, where extra inference can add errors. Free uses are capped.

Grok.t: Act as a coding agent: plan the change, write the code, and explain how to run and test it: {0}
Grok.w: Build in the Grok app or grok.com (limited on free)
Grok.d: xAI lists Grok Build with limited free use. Best for scoped coding jobs; heavy or long-running jobs need a paid plan.
Creates images from text and can edit or combine images you upload. Free daily allowance is small.

Grok.w: No switch: just ask (Imagine; paid plans, limits vary)
Grok.d: Makes a short video clip from a description or image. Full video generation starts on paid tiers (SuperGrok Lite and up); a limited image-to-video clip may appear on free accounts.

Grok.t: Search X (Twitter) posts for what people are saying right now about this and summarise the sentiment.
Grok.d: Taps live posts on X, Grok's distinctive data source. Good for breaking news and public reaction; verify claims independently.

Grok.t: Analyse the attached image and explain what it shows.
Grok.d: Describes or interprets a photo, chart or screenshot you upload. Free upload counts are limited.

Grok.t: Set this up as a recurring Task: {0}
f: What to run, how often, and what to deliver
Grok.w: Tasks at grok.com/tasks (availability varies; a reduced version may appear on free accounts)
Grok.d: Asks Grok to run a query on a schedule and report back. Treat it as a paid feature; if your free account shows a reduced version, you can try it.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Decide how much to reason for this: answer quickly if it is simple, and think longer if it is hard.
Microsoft Copilot.w: Mode selector under the prompt > Smart (some versions label it Auto)
Microsoft Copilot.d: Lets Copilot choose between a fast answer and deeper reasoning for each request. A good default when you do not know which mode to pick.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Answer quickly and briefly. This is a simple question, so skip long explanations.
Microsoft Copilot.w: Mode selector > Quick response (not shown in every version; Smart then decides)
Microsoft Copilot.d: Favours speed for definitions, short summaries and simple conversions.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Take extra time to reason step by step before you answer, and check your work.
Microsoft Copilot.d: Copilot's slower reasoning mode for hard maths, logic, programming and decisions with many variables. Microsoft's support page says use is not limited; paid Microsoft 365 users get priority at busy times.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Teach me this step by step: ask me questions, check my understanding and finish with a short quiz.
Microsoft Copilot.d: A tutoring style for understanding a topic rather than receiving a direct answer.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Search the web for current information and cite your sources.
Microsoft Copilot.d: Grounds the answer in live web results with citations. Use it for news, prices, rules and anything recent.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Run Deep Research on this: plan the research, read many sources and write a detailed report with citations.
Microsoft Copilot.w: Deep Research option in the tools or + menu (name and place vary by app)
Microsoft Copilot.d: Builds a long, cited report across many sources. The free allowance is small and may change, so save it for questions that need it.

Microsoft Copilot.w: No switch: just ask (or the image option in the + menu)
Microsoft Copilot.d: Generates images from a description. Say subject, style and mood. Free allowances can change.

Microsoft Copilot.t: Analyse the attached file or image, summarise the key points and flag anything unclear.
Microsoft Copilot.w: Attach with the + menu, then ask
Microsoft Copilot.d: Reads PDFs, spreadsheets and images you upload and explains or extracts from them. Uploads usually need you to be signed in.

DeepSeek.g: Toggles and modes (under the message box)
DeepSeek.t: Use your most capable model for this task and work through it carefully.
DeepSeek.w: Mode selector under the message box > Expert Mode (Instant Mode is the fast option)
DeepSeek.d: Picks the larger model for harder problems; Instant Mode is quicker for everyday questions. Names and placement can differ between the app and the web.

DeepSeek.g: Toggles and modes (under the message box)
DeepSeek.t: Think step by step and reason carefully before giving the final answer.
DeepSeek.w: DeepThink toggle under the message box
DeepSeek.d: Turns on DeepSeek's thinking (reasoning) mode: slower, but stronger on maths, logic and code. Turn it off for quick or simple tasks.

DeepSeek.g: Toggles and modes (under the message box)
DeepSeek.t: Search the web for current information and cite your sources.
DeepSeek.w: Search toggle under the message box
DeepSeek.d: Lets DeepSeek pull fresh web pages into its answer. It is a manual switch, so turn it on for anything recent, and check key facts elsewhere.

DeepSeek.t: Read the attached document and answer only from it. Say if it does not contain the answer.
DeepSeek.w: Attach with the paperclip, then ask
DeepSeek.d: Summarises or answers questions about PDF, Word and text files. DeepSeek extracts the text, so charts and layout may be lost.

DeepSeek.t: Write the code, explain how it works in plain language, then list edge cases and a few tests.
DeepSeek.w: No switch: just ask (turn DeepThink on for hard problems)
DeepSeek.d: Drafts, debugs or explains code. Asking for edge cases and tests catches the mistakes that quick answers hide.

DeepSeek.t: Solve this step by step, then verify the result with a second method.
DeepSeek.d: Plays to DeepSeek's reasoning strengths; the second-method check catches arithmetic slips.

Meta AI.w: In a WhatsApp or Messenger group chat, type @Meta AI
Meta AI.d: Calls Meta AI into a group chat so everyone sees the answer, for example to settle a question or plan an outing. Needs the Meta app and account. If the pasted text does not trigger it, type the @ yourself and pick Meta AI from the list. Put the question in your core prompt.

Meta AI.t: Use Imagine to create an image of: {0}
Meta AI.w: In Meta AI chats you can also start a message with the word Imagine
Meta AI.d: Creates an image from a description, free, and you can share it straight into a chat or story. Say subject, style and mood. Image features vary by country.

Meta AI.t: Think carefully, step by step, before answering.
Meta AI.w: Thinking or reasoning option in the Meta AI app or meta.ai, where offered
Meta AI.d: A slower reasoning option for harder questions. It is shown only in some regions and app versions.

Meta AI.t: Search the web for current information on this and give me the key points, with links where you can.
Meta AI.d: Meta AI can look things up on the web. Check important facts at the source.

Meta AI.t: Look at the attached image and explain what it shows.
Meta AI.d: Describes or interprets photos and screenshots. Handy for everyday questions such as what a plant is or what a sign says.

Meta AI.t: Write this as a short, casual message I can send in a chat or post on social media. Give me 3 versions.
Meta AI.d: Plays to Meta AI's strength: quick drafts for messages, captions and group plans.
